title: rewrite-ask-to-inbox-check-loop
description:
**Context:** The ask command was reworked in PRD to use an inbox-check loop (no flock) so it can coexist with a running watch. Current implementation calls self.poll() which acquires the flock — making ask incompatible with watch. Reply matching compares UUID field against name string (never matches), and poll auto-marks ALL messages read (violates read-marking principle).

**Goal:** Rewrite ask() to use inbox-check loop with UUID-based matching, marking only the matched reply as read.

**Steps:**
1. In skills/agent-comm/scripts/ac, rewrite the ask() method (line 570-628)
2. Keep the target resolution and online/offline check (lines 580-599) — correct as-is
3. Replace the poll loop (lines 609-627) with inbox-check loop:
   - Use self._poll_req(f"/api/agents/{aid}/inbox?unread=true&limit=50", timeout=30) — NOT poll()
   - Do NOT acquire flock
   - Sleep between checks (5s default)
4. Fix reply matching (line 622): compare msg.get("from_agent") == target_id (UUID) not == to (name)
5. Fix read-marking: after finding match, call self.mark_read(msg["id"]) for ONLY the matched message
6. Add SIGTERM handler: clean exit with exit code 1

**Constraints:**
- Ask MUST NOT use poll() or flock
- Ask MUST NOT mark any message read except the matched reply
- Ask MUST use UUID for reply matching, not agent name
- target_id already holds resolved UUID from _resolve(to) at line 583
- Sleep between inbox checks: 5 seconds

**Acceptance Criteria:**
- [ ] ask uses GET /api/agents/:id/inbox?unread=true&limit=50 (NOT poll endpoint)
- [ ] ask does NOT acquire flock — can run alongside watch
- [ ] Reply matching compares from_agent (UUID) against target_id (UUID)
- [ ] Only the matched reply is marked read — all other messages stay unread
- [ ] SIGTERM handler exits cleanly with code 1
- [ ] Timeout prints "No reply received (timeout)" to stderr, exit 1
- [ ] Target offline prints exact PRD error to stderr, exit 1
close_reason: Completed: ask() rewritten to inbox-check loop (no flock, coexists with watch), UUID-based reply matching, only matched reply marked read, SIGTERM handler

title: webhook-notification-system
description:
**Context:** Hermes agents cannot receive ac watch notifications — background process _reader_loop is broken (docs/HERMES.md). Recommended alternative: agent-comm pushes webhook notifications to hermes' webhook platform with deliver_only mode. Zero LLM cost, sub-second delivery, no background process.

**Goal:** Add webhook notification system to agent-comm so registered agents receive real-time HTTP POST callbacks when messages arrive, enabling hermes webhook platform integration.

**Steps:**
1. Design webhook subscription data model (table, REST endpoints, events)
2. Update PRD.md with webhook architecture section
3. Implement backend: storage, REST API, event emission with HMAC
4. Add CLI commands: `ac webhook register/list/delete`
5. Restructure SKILL.md: shared principles + per-agent guides (Claude Code, Hermes, generic CLI)

**Constraints:**
- HMAC-SHA256 signing mandatory for all webhook POSTs
- Deliver_only mode — POST body IS the notification, no agent processing needed
- Webhook is ADDITIVE — does not replace watch/poll/inbox, agents without webhook support still use ac watch
- Must not block message delivery on webhook failure (fire-and-forget with retry)
- One webhook URL per agent (simple MVP)

**Acceptance Criteria:**
- [ ] Webhook subscription table in DB
- [ ] REST endpoints: POST/GET/DELETE /api/webhooks
- [ ] Event emission fires after sendMessage() for target agents with webhooks
- [ ] HMAC-SHA256 signed POST requests
- [ ] CLI commands: `ac webhook register/list/delete`
- [ ] PRD.md updated with webhook architecture
- [ ] SKILL.md restructured: shared + per-agent sections (Claude Code, Hermes, CLI)
- [ ] Hermes integration documented with webhook config example
close_reason: Completed: webhook notification system — WebhookService, DB migration v7, REST endpoints, HMAC signing, CLI commands

title: backend-webhook-storage-and-rest
description:
**Context:** Epic agent-comm-inh. Depends on PRD spec (agent-comm-myp). Implement webhook subscription storage and REST API endpoints.

**Goal:** Add webhook subscription CRUD — DB table, storage layer, REST endpoints with auth validation.

**Steps:**
1. Create `agent_webhooks` table in storage/schema.sql:
   - id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY
   - agent_id TEXT NOT NULL REFERENCES agents(agent_id) ON DELETE CASCADE
   - url TEXT NOT NULL (validated URL format)
   - secret TEXT NOT NULL (bcrypt hashed)
   - events TEXT DEFAULT NULL (JSON array filter, null = all)
   - created_at TEXT, updated_at TEXT
   - last_success_at TEXT, last_failure_at TEXT, failure_count INTEGER DEFAULT 0
   - UNIQUE(agent_id) — one webhook per agent (MVP)
2. Add storage layer in src/storage/:
   - createWebhook(agentId, url, secretHash, events?) → webhook
   - getWebhooksByAgent(agentId) → webhook[]
   - getWebhook(id) → webhook | null
   - deleteWebhook(id) → boolean
   - updateWebhookStatus(id, success: boolean) — updates last_success/failure_at, failure_count
3. Add REST endpoints in src/transport/rest.ts:
   - POST /api/webhooks — register (validates URL format, agent exists)
   - GET /api/webhooks?agent_id=X — list (never returns secret)
   - GET /api/webhooks/:id — details (never returns secret)
   - DELETE /api/webhooks/:id — unregister (only by owning agent)
4. Add domain logic in src/domain/webhooks.ts:
   - validateWebhookUrl(url) — must be http/https, valid format
   - registerWebhook(agentId, url, secret) — validates, hashes secret, stores
   - rate limit: max 10 webhook POSTs/sec per subscription

**Constraints:**
- Secret stored bcrypt-hashed, never returned in API responses
- Only the owning agent can delete their webhook
- URL validation: must be http:// or https://, max 2048 chars
- Agent must be registered (exist in agents table) to create webhook
- Webhook registration counts as agent activity (heartbeat)

**Acceptance Criteria:**
- [ ] agent_webhooks table created with migration
- [ ] Storage layer with CRUD operations
- [ ] REST endpoints with proper validation and error responses
- [ ] Secret never exposed in API responses
- [ ] Tests for storage and REST layer

title: fix-watch-startup-guard-and-max-unread
description:
**Context:** Watch startup guard should refuse to start if unread count exceeds threshold (default 50, configurable via --max-unread). Currently shows first 20 + warning at >20 and always starts. Missing --max-unread argparse flag. last_seen_id save uses max(all) instead of max(displayed).

**Goal:** Add --max-unread flag, refuse startup when exceeded, fix display thresholds and last_seen_id save.

**Steps:**
1. Add --max-unread argument to watch subparser in main() (near line 819):
   wa.add_argument("--max-unread", type=int, default=50, help="Max unread before refusing start (default 50)")
2. Pass max_unread to watch(): c.watch(args.interval, args.max_unread)
3. Update watch() signature to accept max_unread parameter
4. Rewrite startup guard logic (lines 489-511):
   - If len(new_msgs) > max_unread: print exact error and exit 1:
     Error: too many unread messages (N). Clear your inbox first: ac read-all or ac inbox
   - If 11-max_unread: print header "[WATCH] N unread messages (showing all)" + show all
   - If 1-10: show all (silent)
   - If 0: silent
5. Fix last_seen_id: set to max(m.get("id", 0) for m in displayed_msgs) — only displayed, NOT full list

**Constraints:**
- Error message must be EXACTLY: "Error: too many unread messages (N). Clear your inbox first: ac read-all or ac inbox"
- Exit code 1 on guard refusal
- Default --max-unread is 50 (not 20)
- State file save uses atomic rename (tmp+rename) — already implemented

**Acceptance Criteria:**
- [ ] ac watch --max-unread 10 refuses start if >10 unread
- [ ] Default --max-unread is 50
- [ ] Exact error message matches PRD spec
- [ ] Exit code 1 on guard refusal
- [ ] Display thresholds: 0=silent, 1-10=all, 11-50=all with header
- [ ] last_seen_id = max displayed message ID (not max of all unread)
close_reason: Completed: added --max-unread flag (default 50), startup guard refuses with exact PRD error msg at threshold, last_seen_id now uses max(displayed) not max(all)

title: prd-webhook-notification-architecture
description:
**Context:** Epic agent-comm-inh. Webhook notification system needs PRD specification before implementation. PRD.md currently has no webhook concept — agents can only poll/watch/inbox. Webhook delivery is the recommended real-time notification path (see docs/HERMES.md section 7).

**Goal:** Add webhook notification architecture to PRD.md covering data model, REST API, event emission, CLI commands, and security model.

**Steps:**
1. Add `agent_webhooks` table to Section 3 (Data Model): id, agent_id (FK to agents), url, secret, events_filter (optional, null=all), created_at, updated_at, last_success_at, last_failure_at, failure_count
2. Add new Section 17 "Webhook Notifications" (shift existing 17→18):
   - Architecture overview: agent-comm → HTTP POST → external webhook receiver
   - Event types: message.received (new message for agent), agent.offline (heartbeat lapsed)
   - Delivery: fire-and-forget, HMAC-SHA256 signature, retry up to 3x with exponential backoff
   - Security: HMAC validation, HTTPS recommended, secret rotation
   - Rate limiting: max 10 webhook POSTs per second per subscription
3. Add REST endpoints to Section 12:
   - POST /api/webhooks (register, body: {agent_id, url, secret, events?})
   - GET /api/webhooks?agent_id=X (list subscriptions)
   - GET /api/webhooks/:id (subscription details)
   - DELETE /api/webhooks/:id (unregister)
4. Add CLI commands to Section 10:
   - `ac webhook register <url> [--secret S] [--events message.received]`
   - `ac webhook list`
   - `ac webhook delete <id>`
5. Update Section 17 Known Issues — note watch is deprecated for hermes, webhook is recommended

**Constraints:**
- One webhook URL per agent (MVP)
- HMAC-SHA256 mandatory, no plaintext option
- POST body is JSON: {event, timestamp, agent, data: {message details}}
- Must not block message delivery — webhook emission is async (background task or fire-and-forget)
- Secret stored hashed (like password) — only compared, never returned by API

**Acceptance Criteria:**
- [ ] agent_webhooks table defined in PRD Section 3
- [ ] New webhook section in PRD with architecture, events, delivery, security
- [ ] REST endpoints documented in Section 12
- [ ] CLI commands documented in Section 10
- [ ] Hermes integration example config in PRD or docs/

title: backend-webhook-event-emission
description:
**Context:** Epic agent-comm-inh. Depends on agent-comm-jgb (storage). Implement the actual webhook delivery — when a message arrives for an agent with a webhook subscription, POST the event to the registered URL.

**Goal:** Fire-and-forget webhook POST with HMAC-SHA256 signing when messages arrive for subscribed agents.

**Steps:**
1. Create src/domain/webhook-delivery.ts:
   - emitWebhookEvent(agentId, eventType, data) — looks up webhook, POSTs if exists
   - signPayload(secret, payload) — HMAC-SHA256, returns hex digest
   - buildPayload(eventType, agentId, data) — standard JSON envelope:
     {event, timestamp, agent: {id, name}, data: {message details}}
2. Hook into src/domain/messages.ts sendMessage():
   - After successful message creation, call emitWebhookEvent(toAgentId, 'message.received', message)
   - Async — do not await, do not block message delivery
   - Catch all errors — webhook failure must never affect message send
3. Implement retry logic:
   - 3 retries with exponential backoff (1s, 2s, 4s)
   - Update webhook status on success/failure (last_success_at, failure_count)
   - Disable webhook after 10 consecutive failures (set disabled flag)
4. Add webhook delivery to feed system (src/domain/feed.ts):
   - Emit feed event on webhook registration, delivery failure, webhook disabled

**Constraints:**
- Fire-and-forget: sendMessage() must never be blocked by webhook delivery
- HMAC-SHA256 signature in X-Agent-Comm-Signature header (sha256=<hex>)
- Content-Type: application/json
- Timeout: 5 seconds per POST attempt
- Max payload size: 64KB (truncate message content if needed)
- User-Agent: agent-comm/<version>
- Retry uses setTimeout, not blocking sleep

**Acceptance Criteria:**
- [ ] Webhook POST fires after sendMessage() for target agents with webhooks
- [ ] HMAC-SHA256 signature correct and verifiable
- [ ] Message delivery not blocked by webhook failure
- [ ] Retry with exponential backoff (up to 3 attempts)
- [ ] Webhook auto-disabled after 10 consecutive failures
- [ ] Tests for signing, payload building, retry logic

title: restructure-skill-md-per-agent-guides
description:
**Context:** Epic agent-comm-inh. Current SKILL.md (skills/agent-comm/SKILL.md, 399 lines) is a monolith mixing CLI reference, Hermes-specific integration, Claude Code integration, and troubleshooting. With webhook delivery coming (new notification path), the doc needs restructure for clarity.

**Goal:** Restructure SKILL.md into shared principles + per-agent index sections. Each agent type gets its own focused guide.

**Steps:**
1. Create shared section at top of SKILL.md:
   - CLI location and setup (unchanged)
   - Roles (human vs agents)
   - Common commands: register, heartbeat, send, inbox, broadcast, discover, channels, state, monitoring
   - Key behaviors: auto-heartbeat, auto-mark read, poll lock, config
   - Output format and error format
2. Create per-agent subsections (indexed, not separate files):
   - **Generic CLI Agent** — poll, ask, watch basics. For any agent with terminal access.
   - **Claude Code** — Monitor tool setup, ac watch with grep --line-buffered, identity in .claude/CLAUDE.md, lifecycle (register → Monitor → TaskStop). Reference docs/CLAUDE-CODE.md.
   - **Hermes Agent** — Webhook delivery (recommended), ac watch broken explanation + workaround, deliver_only config example, webhook register command. Reference docs/HERMES.md.
3. Move watch/poll comparison table and anti-patterns to shared section (apply to all agents)
4. Move Hermes-specific troubleshooting (pipe verification, processes.json, gateway restart) to Hermes subsection — keep only high-level pointer in shared section
5. Add webhook commands to CLI reference section

**File layout:**
```
skills/agent-comm/SKILL.md          — shared principles + per-agent index
docs/CLAUDE-CODE.md                  — Claude Code deep guide (exists)
docs/HERMES.md                       — Hermes deep guide (exists)
```

**Constraints:**
- SKILL.md stays as single file (skill discovery expects SKILL.md in skill dir)
- Per-agent sections are concise (2-3 screens each) — deep dives in docs/
- Don't duplicate content between SKILL.md and docs/ — use references
- Keep existing CLI reference format compatible (agents rely on it)
- Hermes section must mention webhook as PRIMARY, watch as legacy/fallback

**Acceptance Criteria:**
- [ ] SKILL.md has clear structure: shared → per-agent index
- [ ] Claude Code section references docs/CLAUDE-CODE.md
- [ ] Hermes section references docs/HERMES.md, recommends webhook
- [ ] Generic CLI section covers poll/ask/watch basics
- [ ] Watch/poll comparison and anti-patterns in shared section
- [ ] No content lost from current SKILL.md — just restructured
